summary.title: Additional resources on Staff-plus engineering
summary.one_liner: A curated reading list of articles, books, talks, and papers recommended for engineers aiming to reach Staff-plus roles, with networking advised as the most valuable resource.
takeaways: Building a network of peers and mentors in similar roles is considered the most valuable learning resource for Staff-plus engineers.
The page groups curated links into sections: role definitions, becoming a Staff engineer, operating as Staff-plus, technical specs, engineering strategy, books, talks, and papers.
Recommended books include A Philosophy of Software Design, Accelerate, High Output Management, The Pragmatic Programmer, and Thinking in Systems.
A list of about 19 foundational distributed systems and CS papers is provided, such as Dynamo, Raft, Paxos Made Simple, and MapReduce, with advice to read 'How to Read a Paper' first.
Papers We Love and Adrian Colyer's The Morning Paper are suggested for finding and following paper summaries.
summary.summary: This is a resource page from staffeng.com collecting recommended material for engineers working toward or operating in Staff-plus roles. It opens by stressing that peer and mentor networks mattered most to the Staff engineers the author interviewed, then lists curated links on role definitions, becoming a Staff engineer, operating at that level, writing technical specs, engineering strategy, and recommended books. It closes with suggested talks (mainly by Cindy Sridharan), a list of foundational computer science papers with guidance on reading them, and a pointer to the author's book Staff Engineer. The page is an annotated link list rather than a tutorial, so depth varies by linked item.
